sm: The hosts open the Thursday, November 19th edition. President Trump tried to calm fears after a string of high-profile tech outages, calling them individual events. He said the press was having fun with it and that nobody would have mentioned such outages under the Biden administration. He added that any country that attacked the United States would know the repercussions. The outages include bank bugs, websites infected with bad code, and a nationwide FAA grounding order after its systems crashed during maintenance. A report says JP Morgan Chase was hit by a cyber attack on third-party vendors, and a ransomware group leaked data on about 16,000 customers. Visa and MasterCard data were also leaked, and the NSA's classified network stayed partly down for a third day. Anthropic then debuted on the stock market, opening at $111.50, 30 percent above its $83 IPO price, at a valuation above $2 trillion. That makes it the largest IPO in history. OpenAI is reportedly eyeing an IPO in 2027.

The Army has a new re-enlistment tactic. Soldiers in Georgia's ninth brigade engineer battalion were offered a four-day weekend to play Grand Theft Auto 6, and 43 re-enlisted. Next, Iowans are seeking answers after a notice warned of toxic lead dust from a planned military detonation at a munitions plant. Maps show possible exposure across more than 50 miles, and residents were told to stay indoors. The UN's International Court of Justice ruled nine to six that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in 2017. It has no way to enforce the ruling. A Van Gogh painting of blossoming chestnut trees sold for more than $190 million at Sotheby's, a new record for the artist. On Guinness World Records Day, attempts included a father and son parallel parking two Minis at once, a portrait of the Statue of Liberty painted in 43.5 seconds, and a BMX backflip. The hosts also recap the day's other stories and say they will return tomorrow morning.
